item.title: Inter star Francesco Pio Esposito sets incredible record as Italy’s most efficient goalscorer in history
item.description: FBL-EUR-NATIONS-ITA-FRA - AFP Inter sensation Francesco Pio Esposito has made Italian football history by recording the best goals-per-minute ratio ever seen for the national team. The young striker has surprisingly surpassed Azzurri legends like Luigi Riva and Silvio Piola with his prolific international strike rate. Setting a new Italian scoring record Esposito has officially written his name into the Italian football history books. The 21-year-old has established the best goals-per-minute ratio ever recorded for the Italy national team. The Inter striker has been in sensational form on the international stage, netting nine goals in just 14 appearances for his country. That includes his two goals during the Azzurri’s 3-1 comeback victory over France at the San Siro. That remarkable return equates to a phenomenal average of one goal every 88 minutes. This astonishing strike rate places the young forward at the very top of Italy's all-time efficiency charts. He has now comfortably outpaced several renowned figures who previously dominated the international scoring rankings. Surpassing former forward Enrico Chiesa To put Esposito's remarkable achievement into perspective, his ruthless finishing has seen him eclipse Enrico Chiesa in the record books. Chiesa previously held a highly respected benchmark, averaging a goal every 91 minutes. However, Chiesa only managed to score seven times during his entire international career with the Azzurri. Esposito has already bypassed that overall tally while maintaining a superior scoring frequency. The third-ranked player on this exclusive list is Julio Libonatti, a striker with dual Argentine-Italian citizenship. Libonatti, who represented Italy between 1926 and 1932, scored 15 goals in 17 games at a rate of one every 102 minutes. Bettering true Italian football legends Perhaps the most impressive aspect of Esposito's record is that he is currently outperforming Italy's greatest ever strikers. Luigi Riva, the all-time leading scorer in the history of the national side, sits further down the efficiency list. Riva famously netted 35 times for the Azzurri, a total unmatched by any other Italian player. Yet, his legendary strike rate stood at one goal every 106 minutes, firmly behind Esposito's current pace. Meanwhile, Silvio Piola, who ranks third on Italy's all-time top scorers list with 30 goals, averaged a strike every 103 minutes. What's next for Esposito? As a player with immense potential, Esposito will now focus on maintaining this historic momentum. Sustaining a goal every 88 minutes over a long career will be a monumental challenge, but the early signs are hugely promising. The 21-year-old must now translate this ruthless international form into consistent club performances to secure a regular starting berth. item.title: Jürgen Klopp praises Brajan Gruda after stunning goal on Germany debut
item.description: Jürgen Klopp praises Brajan Gruda after stunning goal on Germany debut An assist against Manchester City, two against FC Augsburg and now a goal on his debut for the Germany senior national team . Brajan Gruda was named in the starting XI for Germany’s 3-1 win over Serbia in the Nations League, wearing the number ten shirt. Head coach Jürgen Klopp had already described the Leipzig attacker as a “street footballer, simply a brilliant player to watch” ahead of the match. Gruda with a solo run from his own half Operating on the right wing, Brajan repeatedly looked to take on his man against a Serbia side sitting deep. After around 20 minutes, he delivered a pinpoint cross onto the head of Kai Havertz. Shortly after the break, Gruda embarked on a solo run during a spell of Serbian pressure. Receiving a low pass from Joshua Kimmich, he turned away from his marker inside his own half . Approaching the penalty area, he left another defender trailing before slotting a low left-footed finish into the bottom-right corner . Nine successful dribbles on Germany debut - only Jamal Musiala has managed more Against Serbia, Brajan completed nine of his 14 attempted dribbles . According to Opta, only Jamal Musiala has recorded more successful dribbles in a single appearance for Germany over the past ten years. Musiala managed 13 against Costa Rica at the 2022 World Cup. “ It was instinct. I don’t think too much when I’m dribbling with the ball. I just do it . It just happens,” Brajan said of his goal. Klopp summed up the moment in his interview with RTL: “Brajan then calmly put an end to the opposition’s brief resurgence.” Klopp raves about Gruda’s feel for the game “What a debut,” said RTL commentator Wolff-Christoph Fuss as Brajan was substituted off in the 86th minute. Klopp was particularly impressed by the way Gruda switched between keeping things simple and taking on opponents with daring dribbles. “Brajan is an exceptional talent ; he has exceptional ability . The way he mixed things up today, playing simple passes before taking risks again – it was really lovely to watch .” Germany face the Netherlands on Monday evening. Asked whether he could feature in the starting XI again, Brajan replied: “Thankfully, I’ve come through it well. We’ll see what happens.” Discover more Fixtures Red Bull Arena Men's first team Tickets Fan Zone

item.title: Triumphant Democrats descend on COP31 snubbed by Trump
item.description: Fresh from their US midterm election triumph, an emboldened group of Democratic lawmakers descended on the COP31 climate talks shunned by President Donald Trump on Saturday to signal their commitment to tackling global warming. The 18-strong delegation joined the annual UN conference in Turkey after their party regained control of both chambers of Congress in a landslide victory last week cheered by climate campaigners. “Many of our allies and partners across the world think the United States has not been predictable or dependable. So we have a lot of trust to earn back,” Florida Representative Kathy Castor told AFP. “We have so much work to do. And yes, I hope the United States gets back on track with urgent climate action,” she said after the group took photos in front of a large COP31 sign in a sprawling expo centre. The election has been a topic of discussion at COP31 in Antalya, with hopes that Democrats can restore some clean energy policies and that a pro-climate president can be elected in two years. “What happened in the US is remarkable, and a much needed shift that we all needed, not only from a climate perspective, but overall,” Harjeet Singh, strategic advisor to the Fossil Fuel Treaty Initiative, told AFP. Since taking office in January 2025, Trump has rolled back some of the clean energy policies of his predecessors, promoted oil drilling, pulled the United States out of the Paris Agreement and kept his country out of the UN’s climate negotiations. “It is absolutely shameful that the Trump administration operates this way, that this is an administration that is filled with climate deniers, that is beholden to big oil in the United States,” Yassamin Ansari, an Arizona lawmaker, told AFP. – ‘Climate action alive in America’ – Ansari and other members of the delegation spoke at a panel focused on the midterm elections, attracting a crowd that overflowed outside the “America Is All In” pavilion. The group reminded COP31 delegates that, while Trump has rejected clean energy, US states and local governments have continued to promote renewables and other pro-climate policies. A group of US mayors and governors visited COP31 earlier this week, along with former US vice president Al Gore and former US climate envoy and secretary of state John Kerry. “Despite the setbacks that we’re experiencing through this Trump administration, climate action is alive in America,” California Congressman Raul Ruiz told the panel. The president’s Republican party was handed a resounding defeat last week in large part due to anger over soaring energy prices and Trump’s costly war with Iran. Democrats have vowed to use their majority in the House and the Senate to launch investigations into the administration’s climate policies and propose clean energy legislation. But Trump still has two years left in office and has vowed to wield his veto power. “At a time where Americans from all political backgrounds want to see their energy bills reduced, this administrat

item.title: Barcelona president Laporta explains why Lamine Yamal deserves his own legacy: ‘What makes him extraordinary is…’
item.description: Barcelona president Laporta explains why Lamine Yamal deserves his own legacy: ‘What makes him extraordinary is…’ Barcelona president Joan Laporta has delivered another glowing assessment of Lamine Yamal , describing the 19-year-old as a genius while highlighting his exceptional maturity and understanding of the game. However, rather than placing the youngster directly alongside Lionel Messi and Johan Cruyff, Laporta believes Yamal deserves the opportunity to establish his own identity and create a legacy at Barcelona. Speaking in an interview discussing the historic relationship between Barcelona and Ajax, Laporta also reflected on the influence of Cruyff, the importance of La Masia and the club’s ambition to compete for every major trophy. Laporta explains why Lamine is different from Messi and Cruyff Laporta acknowledged that comparisons between Barcelona’s greatest footballing figures and Yamal are inevitable, but insisted that each belongs to a different era. “Each of them is unique and belongs to a different era. Lionel defined a generation, whilst Johan changed the history of both football and Barça,” he began saying. He subsequently explained what makes the teenage forward so special. “He deserves the chance to write his own story and build his own legacy. He is a genius, a very special footballer, with extraordinary technical skills, creativity and an exceptional ability to get past opponents. “What makes him even more extraordinary is his maturity and his understanding of the game at such a young age.” Laporta also stressed the club’s responsibility towards its academy graduate, adding, Laporta has nothing but praise for Lamine Yamal. (Photo by Pascal Le Segretain/Getty Images) “We are incredibly proud that a player of his calibre has come through La Masia and embodies Barça’s values, identity and footballing philosophy. “Our responsibility is to protect him, support his development and create the right sporting environment around him so that he can realise his enormous potential.” He concluded his praise by saying, “As president, I am immensely proud of Lamine, both as a footballer and as a person.” Barcelona president explains La Masia philosophy Beyond Yamal’s individual qualities, Laporta explained that Barcelona’s success must be measured through both trophies and the footballing identity they demonstrate. “At FC Barcelona, our ambition is always to compete for every title – an expectation deeply rooted in our history and our identity. “Our aim is to be in the running right up to the very end in La Liga, the Champions League and the Copa del Rey.” He also emphasised that winning alone is not enough to define the club’s sporting project. “Success is not measured solely by titles. The way we play is also of great importance. Joan Laporta also explained Barcelona’s philosophy. item.title: Kimi Antonelli meets Italian president Sergio Mattarella
item.description: Motorsport photo "To President Mattarella, with great admiration," signed Kimi Antonelli . The new Formula 1 world champion is in the middle of a whirlwind of meetings, events and celebrations for the world title he won two weeks ago at the Mexico Grand Prix, with which he ended a title drought for an Italian driver to win the world championship dating back to 1953. Antonelli, together with his parents Marco and Veronica and his sister Maggie, was received on Friday by the president of the Italian Republic, Sergio Mattarella. The meeting took place at the Quirinale in Rome, with Antonelli giving the president one of his official helmets with a dedication written on the visor. Il Presidente Sergio Mattarella con Kimi Antonelli, Campione del mondo di Formula 1 Il Presidente Sergio Mattarella con Kimi Antonelli, Campione del mondo di Formula 1 Antonelli spoke with the highest office of the Italian state, explaining to him the sensations of wearing a helmet during a race, but also what driving a Formula 1 single-seater entails from a physical point of view. "You lose roughly a couple of kilograms," he said. "We have the fireproof suit, which is also hot. We train to be as ready as we can and to be able to withstand the heat we experience when we drive. But then after the session you jump into a tub of cold water..." The president then asked: "But was it like that in Formula 2 as well? And in karts?" "In karts a little less so," Antonelli replied. "You are much more out in the open. In a single-seater you are enclosed. But in F2 the races last a little less and are less physical. In Formula 1 the race lasts an average of an hour and a half. But will you come and see some races next year? Maybe at Monza? It would be very nice to have you with us." Il casco donato da Andrea Kimi Antonelli al Presidente della Repubblica, Sergio Mattarella Il casco donato da Andrea Kimi Antonelli al Presidente della Repubblica, Sergio Mattarella Mattarella, with a smile, replied: "I really hope so. Now Formula 1 attracts me a lot! The last time was several years ago. It is always complicated, because my movements are complex... But this new situation [referring to Antonelli's competitiveness] greatly encourages me." The meeting with the president was only the latest of Antonelli's engagements. A few hours earlier, Antonelli had attended the match between the Italian men's national football team and the French side, which Italy won 3-1, while the previous day he had stopped in San Marino - where he currently lives - to celebrate the world title. Antonelli will fly back to the United States, this time to Nevada, to contest the third-to-last round of the 2026 Formula 1 season in Las Vegas. item.title: Bruno Fernandes Contract: Manchester United’s Hard To Ignore Problem
item.description: The Bruno Fernandes contract situation has added to the growing list of problems Manchester United are currently facing. The club’s supporters continue to demand the Glazers’ departure, accusing the American owners of having little understanding of how to run a football club. The recent dismissal of Michael Carrick has only added to the uncertainty surrounding Old Trafford. The Englishman becomes the 12th manager, including both interim and permanent appointments, to leave Manchester United since Sir Alex Ferguson’s departure. He also joins an unwanted list of just seven coaches who have lasted less than a year in the role, following his promotion from interim manager to permanent head coach. His departure came after a disastrous start to the campaign, which saw United record their worst league start in 40 years. Now, the Red Devils have appointed Mauricio Pochettino , hoping the former Chelsea and Tottenham coach will finally bring an end to years of instability, restore the club to its former glory and make them genuine contenders in the Premier League title race once again. These problems, alongside questionable recruitment and a lack of squad balance, have exposed just how much work remains to be done at Old Trafford. Despite significant spending in the transfer market, United still have weaknesses in important positions and have struggled to find a consistent goalscorer since Cristiano Ronaldo’s departure in November 2022. There are clearly several issues the club must address, but perhaps the most pressing concerns Fernandes’ United future, with reports claiming that the Man United captain has rejected a second contract offer as his current agreement is due to expire at the end of the season, making the situation even more concerning for the Red Devils. The first offer was reportedly presented during the summer when negotiations began, but the Portuguese midfielder turned it down. His rejection of another proposal suggests that an agreement is still some distance away, leaving United with an important decision to make about one of their most influential players. Ultimately, the Bruno Fernandes contract situation is becoming another major test of Manchester United’s ambition. The club cannot afford to lose another key player while attempting to rebuild its identity and return to the top of English football. If negotiations continue to stall, United could find themselves facing an uncomfortable decision: meet their captain’s demands, or risk losing one of the best players in the Premier League at a time when replacing his influence would be extremely difficult. item.title: Jurgen Klopp urges Germany to embrace "exceptional" quality after Nations League victory over Serbia
item.description: FBL-EUR-NATIONS-SRB-GER - AFP Jurgen Klopp has urged his Germany side to embrace their growing status as a European powerhouse following a dominant 3-1 victory over Serbia in the Nations League. The former Liverpool boss was full of praise for his team's tactical discipline and intensity as they moved a step closer to the quarter-finals. Klopp reflects on dominant display Germany took a significant step toward the Nations League quarter-finals on Thursday night, comfortably dispatching Serbia 3:1 on the road . Reflecting on the dominant display, Klopp insisted that his players must start recognising their own potential as they continue to evolve under his leadership. The result leaves Germany in a strong position in their group, shifting the focus to a high-stakes final fixture in Berlin. "The team played a really, really great game," Klopp told Sky Germany . "I think we have to get used to the fact that we are really good, that we can be really good. To be able to appreciate that correctly: of course we could score more goals today. But I just told the boys: 'I don't really care about that for the moment.' Because we can't say: 'We are starting processes and a development' - and then expect every time we look briefly: 'We must already be further ahead.' Even for ourselves, not just on the outside, for ourselves." Praises total control in hostile Serbia Klopp heaped praise on his side for navigating a hostile away environment unscathed, highlighting their composure as tensions boiled over. Despite facing a struggling Serbia outfit in a notoriously tricky fixture, the German tactician was delighted that his squad avoided any costly injury setbacks while dictating the tempo from start to finish. "It was outstandingly good in so many moments today, so difficult for Serbia, who are certainly not in their best moment. And yet you can really hurt yourself in such games - we didn't at all. So many sequences looked wonderful. In possession we had solutions, were dominant. The counter-pressing was outstanding. Intensity top. So, from my side, a really, really good game," the strategist added. Aggression derailed Germany's rhythm The manager admitted his side lost their rhythm after the break following a sluggish second-half display, noting that his opponents came out with far greater aggression. While his players tried to pick up where they left off, the former Liverpool boss acknowledged that simply attempting to maintain the status quo proved difficult against a team forced to overhaul their approach. However, he was quick to praise Brajan Gruda for calmly stepping up to snuff out the opposition's brief resurgence before the match spiraled. "They came out and were more aggressive. We lacked rhythm. Of course, you could tell we wanted to maintain a rhythm, but then a half doesn't help if you just want to continue as before. The others simply had to do everything differently. item.title: ‘That Would Have Been Nutty’ — Ex-Raiders Boss Makes Feelings Crystal Clear on Trade Rumors Clouding Justin Herbert’s Chargers Future
item.description: ‘That Would Have Been Nutty’ — Ex-Raiders Boss Makes Feelings Crystal Clear on Trade Rumors Clouding Justin Herbert’s Future With Chargers The Los Angeles Chargers have lost their first eight games, falling to 0-8 and becoming the NFL’s only winless team this season. With no wins in the bank, scrutiny is growing around star quarterback Justin Herbert’s place in the franchise, with several former players and analysts calling on the Chargers to tear it all down, trade Herbert, and start afresh. However, former Las Vegas Raiders CEO Amy Trask strongly disagrees with the idea of moving on from Herbert. Justin Herbert Trade Rumors Spark Strong Reaction From Amy Trask Herbert’s struggles were more than evident in the Chargers’ 44-22 loss to the Houston Texans. He completed 13 of 23 passes for 193 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Herbert has gone 144-of-235 for 1,591 yards, six touchdowns and 11 interceptions this season. He ranks at the bottom of the league with a 60.0 PFN QB Impact Grade , and reports indicate Los Angeles did receive a few calls on Herbert’s availability at the trade deadline, with the then-QB-needy Minnesota Vikings among those enquiring. However, Los Angeles had no interest in entertaining any offers, as the franchise continues to see Herbert as its starting quarterback. Trask, it turns out, is not remotely a fan of having that discussion. “I think that the Chargers this season are the biggest surprise in the NFL,” Trask said. “Expectations for the Chargers were very high. I had high expectations for the Chargers. There was muttering that they should look at trading the quarterback. “That would have, in my mind, been nutty as well. I’m mentioning a lot of nutty things, but absolutely don’t trade Justin Herbert. Up until this season, Justin Herbert was phenomenal.” IMPROVE YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free Fantasy Trade Calculator The Texans’ defense also exposed Los Angeles’ offensive problems last week, sacking Herbert eight times in all. He has now been sacked 31 times this season, highlighting the issues plaguing this Mike McDaniel-led offense. Rather than questioning Herbert’s future in Los Angeles, Trask believes the franchise should take a closer look at its offensive approach, especially the work of the offensive coordinator. SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer “He is a good coordinator, but he’s not doing what the best coaches do, which is best positioning players to be their best,” Trask said. “I’ve said for decades that the best coaches don’t take great players or good players or any players and try to push them into a scheme. They build a scheme around the players. “It strikes me that what they’re asking Justin to do is to fit into a scheme for which he’s not best suited. If you’re the coach there, you look at the quarterback, you have Justin Herbert, a terrific quarterback, and you build the scheme around him. item.title: “Are You Gonna Die?” – Alexander Zverev’s Unexpected Comment Toward Journalist Draws Priceless Reaction From Ben Shelton At ATP Finals
item.description: Alexander Zverev © Imagn images Alexander Zverev shared a hilarious moment with Ben Shelton and a reporter during the ATP Finals pre-tournament press conference. Zverev, Ben Shelton, Arthur Fils and Rafael Jodar attended the press conference and a group photo on Friday evening. One journalist told Zverev that he had met all 30 World No. 1 players and that the German player was the last on his list. “I’ve met all 30 No. 1s in the world, and you’re the last one; you’re welcome,” the journalist said. Zverev instinctively responded with a joke, asking: “I’m the last one. Are you gonna die?” Zverev’s response left Shelton in splits; the American was seen hiding his face with his hand and giggling. The ATP Finals will be held from Nov. 15-22. Zverev will face debutant Jodar on the opening day of action at the Inalpi Arena in the afternoon session, followed by a Shelton–Fils clash in the evening. Alexander Zverev on being called the ATP Finals favorite Alexander Zverev and Carlos Alcaraz are the top two seeds at the ATP Finals in Turin. During the pre-tournament press conference for the John McEnroe Group, Zverev shared his view on being referred to as the tournament favorite, saying it is unfair. Zverev added that he is focusing on the challenge posed by Ben Shelton, Arthur Fils and Rafael Jodar. “I think we shouldn’t disrespect anybody,” Zverev said. “I don’t think about Carlos right now. I think about these three young gentlemen because we have a very strong group and everybody shows that they know how to play tennis, otherwise they would not be here. So my focus is on them at the moment and then we see what will happen later in the week.” Zverev also opened up on his approach towards the tournament, adding that he will try to have fun. “How will I approach this tournament? I will approach this tournament with joy,” Zverev said. “I will have fun playing here. I will enjoy being on this court. I will never take it for granted again to be at a spot with the best eight players in the world.” Alexander Zverev won his first two Grand Slam titles this year: the French Open and the US Open. item.title: Real Madrid quartet stand out as Jose Mourinho’s most consistent players this season
item.description: Real Madrid quartet stand out as Jose Mourinho’s most consistent players this season Kylian Mbappe, Jude Bellingham, Marc Cucurella and Yan Diomande have emerged as the only four Real Madrid players to feature in every competitive match before the November international break, making them crucial to Jose Mourinho’s plans. The quartet have all appeared in Real Madrid’s 12 La Liga fixtures and four Champions League matches, but their minutes reveal a clear difference between regular involvement and workload. On that note, the likes of Mbappe and Bellingham have carried the heaviest responsibilities, while Cucurella and Diomande have contributed through a combination of starts and substitute appearances. Mbappe and Bellingham carry the heaviest workload Mbappe leads the group with 1,428 minutes and is the only one to have started all 16 matches. He has completed 12 of those 16 games, which shows just how central the French forward has become to Mourinho’s attacking plans. Bellingham, who is in sensational form this season , follows with 1,305 minutes and 15 starts, having also featured as a substitute on the one occasion he was not named in the starting line-up against Elche. Bellingham has started all but one game for Real Madrid this season. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) Cucurella has accumulated 1,104 minutes through 11 starts and five appearances from the bench. Diomande, meanwhile, has played 891 minutes, starting nine matches and entering as a substitute in the other seven. Diomande makes an impact despite fewer minutes Diomande’s contribution in Europe is particularly notable, as he has recorded two assists and one goal in just 177 Champions League minutes, including a goal in Madrid’s 4-1 victory over Leipzig at the Bernabeu. In fact, during Vinicius’ absence, the former RB Leipzig star performed admirably, forcing Mourinho into a serious rethink once the Brazilian returns to La Liga action after the international break. Similarly, Cucurella’s involvement has also varied considerably. The defender played the entire Madrid derby against Atletico but was introduced only in the 89th minute against Rayo Vallecano. Cucurella’s time has been distributed as a starter and as a substitute. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) He has appeared in all four Champions League matches and provided an assist in the away fixture against AEK Athens. His minutes point to a player whose role can change according to the demands of individual matches. Courtois and Valverde narrowly miss the record Meanwhile, Thibaut Courtois and Federico Valverde are the two players closest to matching the quartet’s appearance record. Courtois has played 1,350 minutes across 15 matches, while Valverde has accumulated 1,181 minutes in the same number of appearances. Interestingly, both have spent more time on the pitch than Cucurella and Diomande, despite missing one of Madrid’s 16 fixtures.

item.title: Olivia Miles reflects on ‘special’ Year 1 with Minnesota Lynx in a heartwarming admission
item.description: Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images Olivia Miles has penned a message following an impressive debut season in the WNBA with the Minnesota Lynx. Miles was one of the top performers in the league and has cemented herself as one of the best rookies in history. She managed 790 points in 2026, which is a new rookie-season record, surpassing the previous total of 769 that was set by Indiana Fever ace Caitlin Clark in 2024. Miles also managed 239 assists for the Lynx in the most recent campaign. She failed to surpass record holder Clark in that area (337) but she still managed to secure the second-most assists of any rookie ever in the WNBA. Now, Miles has taken to Instagram to pen a message about her ‘special’ first year in the league. She wrote: “Finally had the time to realise what the f*** happened this year… “So grateful for the mems, the belief, the love. My circle continues to fuel me and Minnesota welcomed me with such open arms. “I learned a ton – to appreciate the triumphs and failures wholeheartedly. They provide meaning in all of this. But more importantly, to have unwavering faith in my vision. What a special way to spend year 1… can’t wait for the bee hive.” Miles’ Lynx finished first in the WNBA regular season but they failed to make the Finals on this occasion. They lost 2-0 to the New York Liberty in the first round of the playoffs, with Miles scoring 16 points across both games. item.title: Lakers Make Brutal Kevon Looney Assessment Amid 11-2 Start
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers overhauled their roster in the summer, and center Kevon Looney was one of the many new faces they brought in. Looney was set to be the backup to fellow new arrival Walker Kessler , but the Lakers have quickly realized he isn’t up to the task, according to The Athletic’s Dan Woike . “This team really can’t afford to lose Kessler for any extended amount of time,” Woike said. “The Lakers have already decided that Kevon Looney isn’t a workable backup center, and they have limited trade assets to address that (at a time when supply for backup centers is low and demand around the league outside of the Lakers is high).” The Lakers gave up two first-round picks and two first-round pick swaps to the Utah Jazz for Kessler and don’t have much draft capital left now. They can offer a 2032 first-round pick swap and three second-round picks in trades, and that might not be enough to get a quality backup big in this current market. The Lakers just have to hope that the Kessler, who has had a fine start to the season, stays upright. Now, all of the Lakers’ new arrivals haven’t hit the ground running the way he has, but Looney is the only one whose acquisition looks like a clear mistake at this point. The only positive you can point to is that the 30-year-old was given only a one-year, $3.9 million deal . Looney played in each of the Lakers’ first four games, and it appears head coach JJ Redick saw enough in them to take him out of the rotation entirely. The three-time NBA champion has featured in only two of their last nine games and didn’t even play a combined five minutes in them. The Lakers have resorted to playing Jarred Vanderbilt and new arrival Sandro Mamukelashvili at center when Kessler sits. They have done fairly well so far, but you wouldn’t want either of them starting should Kessler go down. This is a bit of a problem for a team that has gotten off to an excellent 11-2 start to the season. Now, it’s not as if no one saw this coming from Looney, who is averaging 1.3 points, 1.7 rebounds, and 0.2 assists per game in 2026-27. He looked like a shell of himself with the New Orleans Pelicans in 2025-26. The Pelicans had signed Looney to a two-year, $16 million deal in 2025, and it would be an understatement to say he didn’t live up to expectations. He averaged 2.8 points, 5.6 rebounds, 1.6 assists, 0.4 steals, and 0.5 blocks per game in 2025-26. Looney only played 21 games for the Pelicans last season, and while injuries played a part, he was also taken out of the rotation simply because he wasn’t playing well. It wasn’t a surprise then that they declined the $8 million team option for 2026-27 and let him hit free agency. The Lakers still signed Looney, and they were warned before the season that relying on him to be the backup center could quickly backfire . item.title: “It Wasn’t Great”: Shohei Ohtani Opens Up Honestly About His 2026 Season After Record-Breaking MVP Top-3 Finish
item.description: Shohei Ohtani - LA Dodgers | © Imagn Shohei Ohtani has offered an honest assessment of his 2026 season, admitting he wasn’t entirely satisfied with his performance despite earning another top-three finish in the NL MVP race. Ohtani finished as the runner-up in the 2026 NL MVP voting after an injury-affected two-way campaign with the Los Angeles Dodgers. Through 14 starts between late March and early July, he looked like a Cy Young contender, recording a 1.79 ERA and striking out 95 batters while holding opponents to a .180 batting average. His final pitching appearance of the season came on July 3 against the San Diego Padres. A recurring left knee issue, along with a right biceps injury, kept him off the mound for the rest of the season and eventually landed him on the 15-day injured list in September. Ohtani continued to play as a designated hitter but struggled to find his rhythm in the postseason, batting .192 with one home run and three RBIs across eight games. Speaking to MLB Network after the MVP results were announced, Ohtani described his campaign as frustrating and admitted that he was unhappy with his overall performance. “No, honestly, I thought it was a very frustrating season, to be quite honest, obviously we did not do that well in the playoffs, personally, I think again, like I said, it was a little bit, frustrated with my overall performance throughout the season, so just in a nutshell, it wasn’t a great season personally for me,” said Shohei Ohtani. He added: “Yeah, I’m truly honoured to be a finalist for the last 6 years, but just even seeing the players who are kind of listed up right now, I do feel truly honoured to be just be in a class with these guys. So it’s great.” Shohei Ohtani finished second behind Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong, who won the award unanimously. The result ended Ohtani’s run of three consecutive MVP awards but extended his streak of top-three finishes to six straight seasons. Shohei Ohtani opened up about what motivates him to improve During the same interview, Shohei Ohtani was also asked what motivates him to keep improving, particularly as he looks ahead to the offseason. Explaining that he does not dwell on his previous seasons or compare himself with past greats, the Dodgers star said he focuses on making the most of each campaign. “Honestly, I don’t really look at my, kind of like my past, how I did in my previous seasons. I truly don’t even look at kind of like compare myself even to some of the past greats, you know, for me, it’s just focusing on each season and to focus on,” said Shohei Ohtani. He added: “Make sure that the season I’m in is like the best season I can make it, and obviously, like I said earlier, we obviously lost in the postseason. So like, again, my focus will just be to make sure we, you know, I perform to the best of my abilities and hopefully win a World Series.” Shohei Ohtani finished the 2026 postseason with a .192 batting average, one home run, three RBIs

item.title: Taylor-Brown wins in Dubai to top T100 standings
item.description: Georgia Taylor-Brown has finished on the podium in all three of her T100 races this season, finishing first in Dubai and Pamplona and third in Vancouver [Getty Images] British triathlete Georgia Taylor-Brown held on to win the penultimate race of the women's T100 season in Dubai and move top of the overall standings. The 2020 Olympic silver medallist claimed her second victory of the season in the fourth event of the campaign, with December's grand final in Qatar remaining. Taylor-Brown will take a six-point advantage over Switzerland's Julie Derron into that final event. The 32-year-old Mancunian, who is a former world champion in the shorter Olympic distance and finished third in this season's World Triathlon Series , is aiming for her first T100 world title. Taylor-Brown won her first T100 race - which includes a 2km swim, 80km bike ride and 18km run - in Spain in May and was third in Vancouver, Canada in August. She hit the front in Dubai just under 4km into the run and opened a 30-second advantage before holding off New Zealand's Nicole van der Kaay to win by just 10 seconds, finishing in three hours 35 minutes and 19 seconds. Derron, who took the lead in the overall standings with victory in Vancouver, was third in Dubai, finishing two minutes seven seconds behind Taylor-Brown. Britain's Kate Waugh, the 2025 champion, was ninth, just ahead of team-mate Lizzie Rayner. Waugh missed the opening two events of the season with a calf injury and is eighth overall heading into next month's Grand Final in Doha.

item.title: US proposed ceding Ukraine territory in exchange for joining NATO
item.description: President Volodymyr Zelensky said that the United States proposed Ukraine cede land to Russia in exchange for joining NATO and that his government was in talks on “specific” security guarantees from the West. Read Also: Trump, Xi, Putin to hold historic meeting in China – White House “The Americans raised a question: ‘What if Ukraine joins NATO? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?’ This was the first time this had been raised,” Zelensky told reporters Friday in comments embargoed until Saturday. He said Ukraine was discussing “specific security guarantees from NATO and the EU” and that if Western countries confirmed them “then I will ask our Ukrainian society what it thinks: do we accept it or not? I have no right to make that decision on my own.” ‘Dangerous’ Ukraine’s Presiudent Volodymyr Zelensky said the EU and NATO are Europe’s only “real security”, warning the Kremlin’s bid to change the continent’s security architecture could lead to more wars. “This is dangerous because, in my view, it is precisely things like this that lead to wars or escalations,” Zelensky told reporters Friday in comments only releasable on Saturday. “Real security in Europe means the EU and NATO. That’s it. There is no other security in Europe.” Russia’ winter war Russia is “betting everything” on this winter’s campaign in its war with Ukraine, President Volodymyr Zelensky said in comments released Saturday as he called for a US military package that would pressure President Vladimir Putin to end the fighting. “They are betting everything on this winter,” Zelensky told the media Friday in comments kept under embargo. He said the US Congress adopting “sanctions and weapons” legislation would be “the kind of motivation Putin needs” to de-escalate. item.title: Jimmy Connors Warns Ben Shelton and Juan Carlos Ferrero of One Major Challenge They Could Face: “Will He Listen?”
item.description: Ben Shelton. © IMAGN via Reuters Connect Tennis legend Jimmy Connors questioned whether Ben Shelton will take advice from Juan Carlos Ferrero, pointing to a potential challenge in their upcoming coaching partnership. Shelton has officially hired former World No. 1 and acclaimed coach Ferrero to join his team for the 2027 ATP Tour season. The news was announced in the first week of November. Unlike his previous full-time role with Carlos Alcaraz, he will work with the American part-time, attending about 12 tournaments each year. His schedule will prioritize Grand Slams, ATP Masters 1000 events, and the ATP Finals, allowing him to spend more time with his family. Ferrero will not replace Shelton’s father, Bryan Shelton. Instead, the two will work together as co-coaches, with Bryan continuing to lead practice sessions and travel with his son to tournaments that Ferrero does not attend. On the latest episode of his podcast, Connors discussed a potential challenge the coaching team could face, questioning whether Shelton would fully trust and listen to the experienced Spaniard. “There is one person who has already proven himself in this relationship, and it’s not Shelton. The question is: will he listen? That’s the problem. Ferrero has proven himself: he has raised Alcaraz to the rank of world number one, and he has already won several Grand Slam titles. He has an undeniable record,” said Connors. He added: “Now, if you recruit a guy like that, will you look at him out of the corner of your eye and ask him, ‘What do you have to bring me?’ Or ‘will you absorb everything like a sponge, take everything and try to trust him?’ It will be interesting.” Ben Shelton last played at the Paris Masters, where he suffered a heartbreaking defeat to Carlos Alcaraz in the final on November 8. Ben Shelton opened up about hiring Juan Carlos Ferrero In a conversation with TNT Sports on November 3, Ben Shelton discussed his decision to bring Ferrero onto his coaching team. Praising the Spaniard’s credentials as both a coach and a former World No. 1, the American highlighted the experience and knowledge he could bring to his career. “He’s a great coach. One of the best coaches in the world. He was also world number one as a player. I think there’s so much experience and wisdom that he can bring to our team and make a big difference for me in my career,” said Ben Shelton. In a recent conversation with Tennis Channel , Shelton also revealed Alcaraz’s reaction after he told the Spaniard he had hired his former coach. Reflecting on the conversation, Shelton praised Alcaraz for his support and sportsmanship. item.title: Surprise stats outline how Man United have missed Casemiro this season
item.description: Surprise stats outline how Man United have missed Casemiro this season Former Manchester United midfielder Casemiro was in sizzling form last season, but it was not enough to convince INEOS to offer him a new deal. The Brazilian was also linked with an exit in the summer of 2025, but ended up staying and delivered a campaign to remember at Old Trafford. The Brazilian finished the season with nine goals and two assists from 35 games. He forged a stellar partnership with Kobbie Mainoo in the second half of the campaign and helped the Red Devils finish third in the Premier League. Unfortunately, with the 34-year-old on the wrong side of 30 and on exorbitant wages at the Theatre of Dreams, the English giants opted to let him go when his contract expired this summer. Casemiro opted to move to Inter Miami, but United’s efforts to fill his shoes at Old Trafford have not gone according to plan so far. United’s midfield revamp has been a disappointment United ended the summer with the purchases of Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba, all candidates with Premier League experience who were expected to hit the ground running at Old Trafford. Unfortunately, the Red Devils have still missed Casemiro this season, with none of the trio managing to replicate his performances in midfield. The English giants have lacked the Brazilian’s instinct for snuffing out danger and protecting the defensive line, as evidenced by the fact that they have conceded 30 goals in 15 games! However, United appear to have missed Casemiro most in the final third, as outlined by a report. Casemiro vs Youri Tielemans vs Carlos Baleba vs Andrey Santos: Stats Page 1 of 3 1 2 3 United have missed Casemiro at set-pieces According to The Athletic , Casemiro’s absence has severely hurt United during set-pieces this season. The report states: “The major statistical detail that stands out, however, is United completely losing their set-piece threat (down from 98 to nine in this ranking system).” “The metric is calculated by expected goals (xG) at set pieces plus goals per 100 set pieces, but weighted 70:30 in favour of xG to reward teams who are generating chances from them but aren’t necessarily scoring.” “A large chunk of United’s drop-off can be traced back to Casemiro. He scored eight goals from set pieces last season – no other player in the squad managed more than two – while he was responsible for around 27 per cent of United’s xG generated from corners.” Casemiro forged a telepathic understanding with Bruno Fernandes, especially at set-pieces, which served United very well. United have underestimated the cost of Casemiro’s departure The report goes on to state that while a departure was always expected due to the finances involved, United may have underestimated the performance cost of Casemiro’s exit. item.title: Verstappen faster than everyone: promising figures for Las Vegas
item.description: Max Verstappen heads to Las Vegas with a second-place finish in Brazil under his belt, where low temperatures are once again expected. An analysis of race pace at Interlagos shows that Red Bull Racing was able to match McLaren and Mercedes in a range of conditions. One particular statistic from the dry phase offers hope for the Dutchman. Verstappen started the Brazilian Grand Prix from 21st on the grid and fought his way up to second place in changeable conditions. Teammate Isack Hadjar finished third, giving Red Bull its second double podium of the year. Conditions played an important role in the result. The race began on a wet track, after which the drivers switched to slicks. Rain returned in the closing stages. These different phases make it possible to compare Red Bull’s performance in wet and dry conditions. The pace on the soft tyres is particularly interesting ahead of Las Vegas, where qualifying and the race are expected to take place in temperatures of around ten degrees. Verstappen faster than McLaren on slicks in Brazil The gaps between Red Bull, McLaren and Mercedes were particularly small during the wet phases. The five fastest drivers on intermediates were separated by just over a tenth of a second. Norris recorded the lowest median lap time, but Hadjar and Verstappen were close behind. Hadjar, in particular, showed that he was comfortable in the changing conditions. Over the entire race on intermediates, the French-Algerian driver was slightly faster than Verstappen and even recorded the best median lap time among the drivers studied during the final spell of rain. The picture changed as the track dried out. Verstappen was the fastest of the eight drivers studied on the soft tyre, with a narrow advantage over Norris and Oscar Piastri. Antonelli was also a few tenths off the pace. Hadjar dropped to fifth in this comparison, more than three tenths behind his teammate. The gaps are small, but they suggest that Verstappen’s performance during the dry phase was not solely down to his charge through the field in the rain. He also had enough pace on slicks to take the fight to the McLarens. One caveat is that tyre age and any delays or difficulties caused by traffic are not factored into the averages, as that data is unavailable. No signs of a major Red Bull disadvantage in tyre degradation The progression of the dry stints also offers some interesting insights. Verstappen completed his first 28 laps on the soft tyre before receiving a fresh set. His median lap time in the second stint was around 1.7 seconds lower. Hadjar gained almost a second and a half on new rubber, while Norris and Piastri also became significantly faster. These improvements cannot be attributed solely to tyre wear. The cars were lighter later in the race, and track conditions changed as well. It is, however, worth noting that these figures do not suggest an exceptionally large drop-off for Red Bull compared with McLaren. This is relevant to Verstappen’s prospects.

item.title: Suspensions over boys' team abusive messages claim
item.description: Some players at Kinsley Boys FC have been accused of sending racist and ableist messages [Getty Images] A boys' football club has suspended a number of players after allegations of racist and ableist abuse against a rival club. Claims of "deeply disturbing and hate-filled messages" being circulated on WhatsApp by members of Kinsley Boys FC followed a fixture with Route One Rovers FC in Bradford on 7 November. Kinsley Boys FC confirmed on Friday that a number of its players had been suspended pending the outcome an investigation. A spokesperson said the team was working with the Football Association (FA) and Northern Counties East Football League to ensure the matter was investigated "thoroughly, fairly and in accordance with the relevant regulations". "The club does not condone discrimination, abusive behaviour or conduct that falls below the standards expected of anyone representing Kinsley Boys FC. "We remain committed to ensuring that all individuals involved are treated fairly and that appropriate action is taken following the conclusion of the investigation," they said. A statement from Route One Rovers FC said it condemned the "vile racist, Islamophobic, discriminatory and abusive language" contained within messages reportedly shared in a Kinsley Boys FC players group chat. These included offensive comments directed towards a wheelchair user on the management team and Islamophobic comments about players, it said. A spokesperson from the club said: "This is not football banter. This is discrimination, and it is utterly unacceptable. "Such behaviour has absolutely no place in football or wider society." The club said it had also experienced racism last season and thanked the community for its support and solidarity. Kinsley Boys FC said it was co-operating with the relevant football authorities, including the FA and the Northern Counties East Football League. A spokesperson for the Northern Counties East Football League confirmed it had received a formal complaint concerning alleged discriminatory comments circulated via a private messaging group. "The allegations are extremely serious and include claims of racism, religious discrimination, disability discrimination and abusive conduct. "The matter has been formally recorded and referred to the appropriate authorities for investigation. The NCEL is committed to ensuring that football is inclusive, respectful and welcoming to all," they said. Football inclusion charity Kick it Out said it was "appalled" by the reports. "Discrimination has no place in football at any level, and we stand with everyone affected. "Our reporting team is aware of the incident and is working with the relevant authorities to ensure it is investigated and that those responsible are held accountable," a spokesperson said. item.title: Microsoft's school email bill gives rivals something to smile about
item.description: The fallout from Microsoft's education price rises and service cuts continues as institutions weigh the prospect of bigger bills, and the Windows maker's rivals struggle not to pull "I told you so" faces. The main takeaways are that free student email and collaboration services are being retired, and storage entitlements are changing. These changes generally apply at institutions' first renewal or extension on or after January 1, 2028. Microsoft announced the new plans last week, and the UK's Department for Education described itself as "disappointed" at the news. As well it might be, although the UK government has rarely seen a deal from Microsoft that it didn't like . Or, for that matter, other US tech giants . Exactly how much educational institutions will have to spend remains unclear. Mary Jo Foley of Directions on Microsoft put indicative student pricing at $2 per year for Microsoft 365 Education A2, $4 for A3, and $6 for A5, with Teams adding another dollar annually. Faculty licenses cost considerably more, while the new A7 student tier jumps to $385 a year before Teams. Foley cautioned that these were approximate figures, with actual prices set by Microsoft's partners. The new no-cost student tier, Microsoft 365 Education A0, is a poor replacement for Office 365 A1: it excludes Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, and Teams. Eligibility also requires full paid faculty coverage on A2 or higher and students who actively use Windows devices for education – potentially awkward for institutions running fleets of Chromebooks. A few dollars per student might not sound alarming. Multiply that across an institution, however, and something that used to be free becomes a recurring bill. Michael Meeks, CEO of Collabora Productivity, told The Register: "Free was the bait on the hook, and Microsoft spent years reeling in schools' email accounts, documents, identity management and classrooms onto its cloud." A poster on the edugeek.net forums commented: "This was always going to happen, I remember thinking this when we moved over to the MS free cloud solution. It will be free until they decide it isn't." The risk for Microsoft is that there are options. Meeks told us: "Schools now have a year to plan, and, in our experience with other large-scale educational projects, such as the University of Lille, that can be enough time to migrate properly." Other options include Nextcloud, which will be rolled out as part of Germany's Educational Cloud Infrastructure . Several Swiss universities also migrated to the service over an August weekend. According to Nextcloud, 39,500 students, teachers, and researchers, along with 585 terabytes of data, were shifted. Both Nextcloud and Collabora Productivity also highlight another factor that could drive educational institutions away from Microsoft: sovereignty. item.title: I can never insult Peter Obi; we parted ways amicably — Tanko
item.description: By Henry Umoru, Abuja The National Coordinator of the Social Democratic Party, SDP Presidential Campaign Council, Dr Yunusa Tanko, has taken a swipe at those behind viral reports circulating online alleging that he spoke ill of and used unprintable words against the candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, ahead of the January 16, 2027 election, Peter Obi, saying he cannot ever insult his former principal. The National Coordinator of Prince Adewole Adebayo and Dr Usman Bugaje’s Presidential Campaign Council described the fabricated reports as the desperate handiwork of those he described as mischief-makers and political detractors bent on sowing discord and tarnishing his hard-earned reputation. In a statement signed on Saturday by the Chief Media and Communications Advisor, Adebayo-Bugaje (Ade-Buga) Presidential Campaign Council, Comrade Mark Adebayo, Tanko explained that anyone familiar with his character and political journey knows that he is a principled, decent, and respectful individual who neither engages in blackmail nor trades in insults. He expressed complete confidence that Peter Obi would immediately dismiss the falsehoods, knowing full well the mutual respect they share. “I can never insult His Excellency, Mr Peter Obi,” Dr Tanko stated emphatically. “We parted ways peacefully and with absolute mutual understanding. Politics is about vision and service, never about bitterness or personal attacks.” Reiterating the sentiments he shared during his unveiling as the National Coordinator of the Adebayo-Bugaje Presidential Campaign Council, Dr Tanko expressed deep appreciation and lasting gratitude to Mr Obi for the relationship they shared during his tenure as an aide and as the National Coordinator of the Obidient Movement Worldwide. “I remain forever grateful to His Excellency, Mr Peter Obi, for the wonderful opportunities he gave me to serve alongside him and lead the Obidient Movement worldwide. I thank Mr Obi, and I stand proudly by the records of my service with him,” he added. Dr Tanko, who warned purveyors of fake news that their attempts to manufacture bad blood between him and his former principal have failed before arrival, affirmed that he and the 2023 presidential candidate of the Labour Party (LP) remain the best of friends and pledged that he will continue to accord the former Anambra State Governor the utmost respect at all times. The Adebayo-Bugaje Presidential Campaign Council urges the general public and members of the press to disregard the malicious publications in their entirety and rely only on verified communications from the council. item.title: Lisandro Martínez Handed "Confidence" Blow On International Duty
item.description: Does Mauricio Pochettino need to sign a new centre-back? Lisandro Martínez has come under criticism in recent weeks, despite being heavily praised for speaking out in the post-match interview in Madrid. The Argentine was sent off for two yellow cards in the space of just over one minute against Chelsea , which saw him dropped to the bench for the Champions League tie against AS Roma. Martínez and Shea Lacey came on together in the second half, but while Lacey received a cheer, Martínez was booed on – something rarely seen at Old Trafford. Martínez was called up for international duty as Argentina faced Uruguay in their first match. The Manchester United defender played all 90 minutes, but his side lost 2-1, and the Argentine media were not impressed by his performance. Argentine media react to Martínez's performance Martínez started alongside Leonardo Balerdi, and was not at his best when his centre-back partner netted an own goal. TyC Sports , a well-known Argentine outlet, said after the game that Martínez was "not enjoying" his football at Manchester United , and it showed in his performance. "He’s not enjoying his best form at United, and it showed somewhat in his confidence and understanding with his centre-back partner," they said as Martínez was handed a 5/10 rating. "While he didn’t make any major errors, his involvement in Uruguay’s first goal wasn’t his best and didn’t live up to his other excellent performances. "He had to be overly alert in his tackles due to Balerdi’s poor positioning." Pochettino will be disappointed to hear of Martínez's poor performance, but will be hoping he can turn his countryman's form around. Nicky Butt has already described their relationship as "interesting." Premier League Legend Tips Michael Carrick For Championship Job After Man Utd Sack Alan Shearer defends the ousted manager’s reputation, insisting the Old Trafford icon remains a prime candidate for immediate coaching roles despite United’s recent slide into the relegation zone. Martínez on last Man Utd chance Since his comments after the 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid, there have been some suggestions that Martínez wants out of Old Trafford. But whether he likes it or not, he has been given one final chance to impress at Manchester United. Mauricio Pochettino will have Martínez available for the trip to Anfield, as he was only handed a one-game suspension for his red card at Stamford Bridge, though Harry Maguire and Matthijs de Ligt are among the few who have not been called up to international duty. Ayden Heaven and Leny Yoro will also be hoping for regular game time under the new boss, though Pochettino may favour experience over youth as he looks to bed in a new style of play. The former Spurs head coach has been known to choose young players: during his time at Tottenham Hotspur , he handed more debuts to players aged 21 or under (21) than any other manager. With that in mind, Martínez will know he needs to impress from the very start if he wants t

item.title: Times Shield is an institution, says Amol Muzumdar
item.description: MUMBAI: India women’s cricket team head coach Amol Muzumdar urged young cricketers to respect the game, embrace failure and put the team first at the Times Cricket Shield prize distribution function at the MCA Lounge, Wankhede Stadium, on Friday. Recalling his early days in Mumbai cricket, Muzumdar spoke about the advice he received from former India batter and 1983 World Cup winner Sandeep Patil when he made his Times Shield debut for Sungrace Mafatlal in 1993. The Times Award Shield was sponsored by The Times of India Cricket Shield’s celebration partner Heineken 0.0 (Mr. Vasant Bhandari) and Sterling Reserve Packaged Drinking Water. Incidentally, this is the 96th year of the Times Shield, which started in 1930. “Score 200. What’s the big deal about scoring 100? Everyone here scores hundreds. If you have the guts, score a double hundred, then I’ll accept it,” Patil had told him. The words motivated the then 18-year-old, but his debut innings ended at 97. “As I was walking back, the captain was sitting in front of me. He gave me a smirk. That was my baptism of fire in Mumbai cricket,” Muzumdar recalled. Three months later, he scored a then world-record 260 on his firstclass debut for Mumbai against Haryana in a Ranji Trophy pre-quarterfinal in Feb 1994. Muzumdar, who went on to captain Mumbai and score 11,167 runs in 171 first-class matches, offered three lessons to youngsters. “Respect the game. That is the most important thing. The game will respect you back multifold,” he said. He also urged players not to fear failure. “Failures are part of every cricketer’s life, it’s only a question of how you respond,” he said. Highlighting the importance of the Times Shield in Mumbai cricket, Muzumdar said, “The Times Shield has been an integral part of Mumbai cricket. But I can tell you one thing: It was an absolute privilege to play in the Times Cricket Shield when I first started. It’s not just a tournament, but an institution. It is probably the livelihood of so many cricketers. It gave a platform, an encouragement to so many cricketers to display their talent. “It was just an honour to play in the Times Shield when I started and even when I finished in 2013.” Former India batter and BCCI Cricket Advisory Committee member Jatin Paranjape, the other chief guest, lauded the tournament’s role in strengthening Mumbai’s club cricket. item.description: ‘Throwing J.J. (McCarthy) Under the Bus?’ ‘This Guy Is a Nightmare’ — NFL Fans Read Between the Lines on Malik Nabers’ Assessment of Giants’ Loss to Commanders The New York Giants’ 24-21 loss to the Washington Commanders on Thursday night left a bad taste in the mouth, but Malik Nabers’ comments the following day only added to the drama. The wide receiver questioned the team’s late-game decisions, leading some fans to believe he was blaming quarterback J.J. McCarthy rather than owning up to his own mistakes. Malik Nabers Questions Giants’ Late-Game Decisions After reaching Washington’s 48-yard line with 42 seconds remaining, McCarthy attempted a short pass to Malachi Fields before taking consecutive deep shots toward Darnell Mooney and Malik Nabers. He acknowledged that his mistake cost the Giants a potential scoring opportunity and said he needed to improve his ball security and awareness. item.title: SpaceX's Starship encounters problems during 15th test flight
item.description: Elon Musk’s SpaceX successfully launched its Starship, the world's largest spaceship, into orbit where it should release 15 satellites for its Starlink network. A few minutes after lift off however, the rocket's booster which was meant to return to the pad splashed down in the Gulf of Mexico. Details by Daniel Quinlan.

item.title: Who Gets To Compete?
item.description: Opposition talks are continuing. Campaigns are gathering pace. But access, legal certainty and confidence in the vote are becoming defining questions of the election. In Yelwata, Peter Obi stood before a community carrying the wounds of mass violence. In Akure, the APC called its organisation to work for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election. In London, INEC’s chairman faced questions about whether Nigerians could trust the coming vote. These were different settings for the same election. Together, they reveal a contest in which persuading voters is only part of the task. Candidates must sustain their organisations, establish their right to participate and reach citizens safely. The electoral commission must demonstrate that those citizens’ choices will be recorded faithfully. The week’s developments sharpen a fundamental question: how open, credible and competitive will the road to 2027 remain? Lagos Raises the Stakes Thursday’s reported attack on an NDC town hall gathering in Oregun, Lagos, deserves particular attention. According to reporting from the scene, armed men disrupted the gathering, participants were injured and a suspect was arrested. The NDC alleged political responsibility; the Lagos APC denied sponsoring the incident. The report established no independent evidence linking the attackers to a political party. Investigation must establish who acted, who organised them and whether anyone provided support. The democratic principle requires no such delay: citizens must be able to attend lawful political meetings without fearing assault. Violence can influence an election before a ballot is cast. It can discourage attendance, make venues reluctant to host meetings, increase campaign costs and persuade volunteers to stay home. Its effects therefore extend beyond the immediate victims. When intimidation restricts participation, it changes the conditions under which candidates compete. Political leaders should condemn attacks consistently, including when the victims support their opponents. Security agencies must provide protection on the same basis. Makinde Keeps the Alliance Door Open Seyi Makinde’s latest comments give fresh substance to the opposition’s continuing conversation about cooperation. In an interview reported today, the Oyo governor confirmed active discussions involving Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi. He said decisions should draw on evidence, manifestos, previous performance and public sentiment. He did not announce an agreement or endorse a preferred candidate. That distinction separates a development worth watching from a coalition already formed. The negotiations face a familiar practical difficulty: cooperation requires choices that impose costs on participants. Someone may need to surrender an ambition, accept another candidate’s leadership or persuade supporters to work with former rivals. An agreement also needs to travel beyond the negotiating room. item.description: The Financial Times says computing giant Nvidia has approached Rene Haas, CEO of British chip designer Arm, in its search for a potential successor to Jensen Huang. Huang resigned after his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Meanwhile some employees are clamouring for Huang's return – as his fellow tech leader Elon Musk. item.title: Barcelona reach agreement with 20-year-old versatile midfielder over new contract until 2031
item.description: Barcelona reach agreement with 20-year-old versatile midfielder over new contract until 2031 Barcelona are closing in on another important contract renewal, with Brian Farinas reaching a preliminary agreement with the club over an extension that could keep him at Camp Nou until 2031. According to MARCA , sporting director Deco has held several meetings with the versatile midfielder’s representatives in recent weeks, with negotiations progressing towards a final agreement. Barcelona want to reward the youngster’s development after his promotion to Hansi Flick’s first-team squad and protect his future amid growing interest in emerging European talent. It is to be noted that Farinas’ existing contract runs until 2028 and reportedly includes a €15 million release clause. The new agreement, on its part, is expected to increase his protection against approaches from other clubs, although the official number is yet to be disclosed. Deco accelerates negotiations after Farinas’ first-team breakthrough Farinas will renew his Barcelona contract until 2031. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Barcelona’s intention to renew Farinas’ contract dates back to the end of August, when the club decided to promote him to the first team and assign him a senior squad number. Negotiations began around that time but gathered momentum towards the end of October following his first-team debut against Alaves. As a result, the sporting department consequently moved to improve his financial package while also securing a longer commitment. As stated before, the proposed agreement would extend Farinas’ stay by three years, taking his contract from 2028 to 2031. As per the outlet, although a shorter extension was also discussed, that possibility was eventually discarded. Farinas was close to joining Girona in the summer. (Photo by Pedro Salado/Getty Images) Considering the recent development, Barcelona are now preparing to formalise the arrangements. Barcelona protect their emerging first-team talent Farinas’ renewal is part of a strategy where Barcelona want to ensure the club’s emerging players have contracts reflecting their growing importance. On that note, the club has already secured Raphinha’s future until 2030, while Marc Bernal and Gerard Martin are also part of the sporting department’s renewal planning. Lastly, it is crucial to remember that Farinas was close to leaving Barcelona in the summer, with Girona emerging as the most likely destination. Flick, however, decided to keep the player, and although it took a while, Farinas has finally made his Barcelona debut and is tipped for gradual progression.

item.title: “Lots Of Negative Talking Towards Me” – Elina Svitolina Reveals Current Relationship With Gael Monfils Amid WTA Finals & Marriage Split
item.description: Elina Svitolina © Imagn Elina Svitolina has spoken up about her current relationship with Gael Monfils. Svitolina and Monfils became one of tennis’ most high-profile power couples after starting to date in late 2018, and they married three years later. However, in October this year, they released a joint statement confirming their divorce. The announcement led to significant fan backlash against Svitolina, with critics particularly finding fault with her citing the war in her native Ukraine as one of the reasons for ending the marriage. Monfils, considered one of the ATP Tour’s greatest entertainers and a popular locker-room player, hung up his racket earlier this year. However, Svitolina’s WTA career continues to thrive. The Ukrainian veteran is currently competing at the WTA Finals, where she has advanced to the semifinals. Here, she was interviewed by journalist Christian Basnight, who asked the World No. 6 whether she views the year-end championships as an ‘escape’ from the turmoil in her personal life. Dismissing the suggestion, Svitolina told Basnight : “I wouldn’t say so (that the 2026 WTA Finals has been an escape for me) because still lots of things are going on. Social media, a lot of pressure and I think lots of negative talking on social media towards me. I wouldn’t say it’s an escape in a way because in this situation I just want to be away from the media and all the social media. I try to deal with it the best way I can.” She also said that her relationship with Monfils, despite their divorce , remains positive, and that their shared priority is ensuring the happiness of their daughter, Skai. Svitolina added: “I have great people around me and most importantly, I think just being honest with you guys, we have a great relationship with Gael. Even 10 minutes before the match I had to talk with him and we’re on good terms. The most important thing for us is to have our daughter happy. It’s the most important priority for us.” Elina Svitolina storms into the WTA Finals’ last four with a win over former World No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka Svitolina’s 2026 WTA Finals campaign did not get off to the best of starts, with the Ukrainian suffering a chastening straight-set loss to Mirra Andreeva. However, she kept her chances of progress alive with a three-set win over Karolina Muchova in her second Round Robin phase outing. It all boiled down to the Ukrainian’s last Round Robin stage outing against former No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka. Quite simply, the winner would progress to the semifinals and the loser would go home. Here, Svitolina produced a gritty display, ultimately registering a 6-3, 3-6, 6-1 win to down the four-time Major singles champion from Belarus . Up next for Svitolina is a semifinal showdown against reigning Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova. The winner of the last-four match will face either Mirra Andreeva or Jessica Pegula in the final. item.title: 'I'll be surprised if he's still there!' - Gary Lineker's brutal warning to Mauricio Pochettino over Man Utd job
item.description: United States Training in St. Paul - Getty Images Sport Gary Lineker has sensationally warned Mauricio Pochettino that his reign as Manchester United manager is ultimately destined to end in failure. The former England striker believes deep-rooted structural problems at Old Trafford mean the Argentine will struggle to survive beyond 18 months. Lineker issues stark Pochettino warning Pochettino faces a monumental task at United after signing a two-and-a-half-year deal to succeed Michael Carrick . The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss inherits a squad severely lacking in confidence following a disastrous start to the campaign. The Red Devils currently languish in 18th place in the Premier League table. They are without a top-flight victory in eight matches, a miserable run that dates back to late August. While many expect the Argentine to deliver a highly anticipated new manager bounce, Lineker holds serious reservations about his long-term prospects. The outspoken pundit believes the Old Trafford hierarchy will inevitably set Pochettino up to fail. A strict eighteen-month survival timeline Speaking on The Rest Is Football podcast, Lineker predicted a familiar pattern of brief optimism followed by inevitable disappointment. He claimed that the systemic issues within the club will quickly overwhelm their latest managerial appointment. "I see Pochettino going in there, and I think they’ll probably get off to a reasonable start, and they’ll do okay for a while," Lineker explained. "‘I think for Pochettino, it’s a big club, Manchester United, big by name. He’ll go on there, and then he’ll be disappointed with the way things occur in the future, and if he’s still there in 18 months, I’ll be surprised." Ownership problems continue to mount Pochettino becomes the latest in a long line of high-profile managers tasked with restoring United to their former glory. Lineker pointed out that 12 different coaches have now passed through the doors since Sir Alex Ferguson retired, with almost all leaving under a dark cloud. He also defended Carrick's recent tenure, pointing the finger directly at the recruitment team. "Because again and again, it’s rinse and repeat; the scapegoat is always the coach, and you can see that," he added. "And I think the real problems are above the coach. These guys are all good coaches. You look at some of the names they’ve had in the last 10 years. What’s that, 12 coaches now who have gone since Alex Ferguson? And they all leave and they say the club’s a mess. "There will always be coaches to blame, and they didn’t back Carrick properly in the summer. They didn’t. He performed brilliantly in the second half of last season. Admittedly, they weren’t in European football, and they were playing counter-attack stuff, but I don’t know how long the people at the top of Manchester United can get away with it. And ultimately, I think the fans know anyway. "Obviously, there have been years and years of complaints and demonstrations against the

item.title: Connecticut football's numbers keep falling. Coaches say rebuilding starts long before high school
item.description: New Canaan football head coach Lou Marinelli celebrates with his players following their win over Cheshire to capture the CIAC Class L state championship Saturday, December 13, 2025 at Veterans Stadium in New Britain. (Jim Shannon/Hearst Connecticut Media) Lou Marinelli hit his exercise bike hard Monday morning. The New Canaan football coach had a big week ahead. Unbeaten St. Joseph was coming to town Friday and Marinelli's Rams were coming off their first loss in 29 games . Time to get back in the saddle and get the wheel back in spin. That's just short term. As Connecticut's longest-tenured and winningest coach knows full well, CIAC football faces a long-range challenge, and that's halting a decade-long decline in player participation . Connecticut has gone from approximately 10,000 high school football players in 2013 to 8,000 in 2025. While a final total is not yet in for 2026, many teams are showing smaller numbers this fall, several rosters have dropped into the low 20s, and two teams, Derby and McMahon, postponed games for a lack of healthy numbers. "The #'s of students in football has been dropping for the last decade," former Hartford Public coach Harry Bellucci posted on X when last week's McMahon-Trumbull game was postponed . "Whether it's CTE concerns, too many athletes focusing on just one sport, video games or social media, it's a continuing trend that needs to get reversed or a whole lot more co-ops. That will be the norm soon." @GametimeCT @MetalNED The #'s of students in football has been dropping for the last decade. Whether it's CTE concerns, too many athletes focus on just one sports, video games or social media. Its a continuing trend that needs to get reversed or a whole lot more Co ops. That will be the norm soon. - Harry Bellucci (@coachbellucci) October 30, 2026 It's the norm right now. Nine co-ops have sprung up in the past two years, raising the CIAC total to 26 , doubling the 13 that were around in 2013. Coaches and athletic directors acknowledge more co-ops are likely in the future, especially among city schools and small suburban and rural districts. In the meantime, they say, steps can be taken to counter current trends: • Greater integration between high school and youth football programs. • Greater selling of the game in the schools by coaches. • Greater community, parental and administrative support. It's very much a vertical alignment, which is apropos. Many of the factors underlying the situation are arguably economic in nature. "Times are tough: We get that a lot from parents," said Nonnewaug Co-op coach Scott Lynch, who's had some players torn between football and part-time jobs. Platt head football coach Jason Bruenn during their game against Berlin at Falcon Field in Meriden Thursday, November 12, 2026. item.title: US nationwide flight ground stop: "Our routers got overloaded with data"
item.description: On Friday, the Federal Aviation Administration issued a rare nationwide ground stop. More than 8,200 flights, or over 31% of those scheduled in the United States, were canceled. The ground stop lasted nearly five hours and was the longest in the country since September 11, 2001. Officials blamed outdated air traffic communications equipment, and said that there was no evidence of a cyber attack. The airspace is now reopened and flights have resumed.
